mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) over the prior three months compresses the risk-free rate, reducing the discount rate applied to equity valuations and generating positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods where FEDFUNDS declines by at least 0.25 percentage points over the prior three months.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) rises above 4.5% in a single month, it signals deteriorating labor market conditions that reduce consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of months where UNRATE exceeds 4.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent decline in housing starts (HOUST) and industrial production (INDPRO) over the prior two months indicates a broad-based economic contraction that erodes corporate profit expectations, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST and INDPRO both decline > 0.5% from prior month
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances where both HOUST and INDPRO decline by more than 0.5% from the prior month.

mechanism_narrative: In monetary tightening cycles (FEDFUNDS > 4.5% and rising for two consecutive months), higher interest rates reduce corporate leverage and consumer credit availability, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods meeting the monetary tightening cycle definition (FEDFUNDS > 4.5% and rising for two months).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in non-farm payrolls (PAYEMS) over the prior three months signals robust labor market conditions that support consumer spending and corporate earnings growth, generating positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods where PAYEMS increases by at least 0.5% over the prior three months.

mechanism_narrative: When housing starts (HOUST) fall below 1300.0 thousand units in a single month, it indicates a weakening housing market that reduces consumer wealth and construction sector activity, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of months where HOUST falls below 1300.0.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in real personal consumption (RSAFS) and rise in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) over the prior month indicates a contraction in consumer demand amid monetary tightening, which erodes corporate revenue growth and triggers negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS declines > 0.5% and FEDFUNDS rises > 0.25% from prior month
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances where RSAFS declines by more than 0.5% and FEDFUNDS rises by more than 0.25% from the prior month.

mechanism_narrative: During periods of industrial production contraction (INDPRO declining for two consecutive months), the S&P 500 experiences negative returns over the next 60 days as manufacturing weakness signals broader economic deceleration and reduced corporate capital expenditure.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods where INDPRO declines for two consecutive months.
